analysis: Two changes were examined. (1) StartCommand+Modes.swift head lines 216-217: runForeground now calls attachWeightHashes(to: combined, verifiedWeightHashesFile: VerifiedWeightHashStore.path()), where the base called attachWeightHashes(to: combined). The hashes still feed ProviderLoopConfig.modelHashes and modelHashFingerprints, and autopilotInventory filters on a non-empty weightHash. The new VerifiedWeightHashStore and the changed attachWeightHashes overload are not supplied, so I could not confirm the semantics. This is relevant to T-012 (weight substitution), T-027 and the weight-hash binding behind T-041 (the SSD cache is bound to the verified weightHash). Open questions for integration: where the store lives (a user-writable path could let the operator pre-seed trusted hashes, though the operator is already adversarial and the coordinator's weight-hash verification is the authority); whether a stale or missing cache entry fails closed (empty hash) rather than reporting an unverified hash; and whether the file is read with no-follow or ownership checks. No concrete regression is visible from the diff, since the store implementation is unavailable. (2) StartCommand.swift head lines 173-179: a new GLMWiredLimitAdvice.startNotice call computes advertisedModels and prints a warning to stderr. It is advisory only, writes nothing and sends nothing over the network, and does not alter serving authorization or the model set actually served. It adds a duplicate advertisedModels evaluation before mode dispatch, and the snapshot-derived hardware data in the notice is local only. The local-mode, token and fail-closed logic is unchanged, and no change touches the attestation, App Attest, WebSocket or encryption paths. The next pass should review VerifiedWeightHashStore and attachWeightHashes for path trust and fail-closed behavior.
